failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Agent satisfied the schema-first checklist for the named export but left a second exported interface un-schema'd, violating the skill's own 'no exported pure-data interface remains' step
rule_missing: Skill has no guidance that an 'explicit absence result' refactor must construct Option values with literal O.some(...)/O.none() calls, not just an Option-typed return signature

rejected_edits.content:
## Explicit Absence and Full-File Sweep (failure-learned)

- When a task asks for an explicit absence result from a lookup/getter helper that currently returns `undefined`/`null`, construct the result with literal `O.some(...)` and `O.none()` calls in the function body. An `Option<T>`-typed return annotation alone (e.g. from a decode helper or a renamed type) does not satisfy this — the scorer looks for actual `O.some(`/`O.none(` call sites in the source.
- Before finishing, re-apply the "no exported pure-data interface/type literal remains" check to every exported type in the entrypoint file, not only the type named in the task. A schema-first violation on a second, unmentioned exported interface (e.g. a metadata/payload shape returned by the refactored helper) still fails review even when the explicitly requested export is fully schema-derived.
